A1.justification: Both complete 18-page PDFs describe POLAR, with the same title, main sections, and supplementary material. Text extraction and visual comparison support reliable comparison of the figures, tables, equations, and appendices.

before.justification: v4 reports original POLAR evaluations on three datasets, computational measurements, ablations, and supplementary robustness and generalization experiments.

after.justification: v5 retains these original POLAR benchmark results, computational measurements, ablations, and supplementary experiments.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical radar aggregation, MDE-radar fusion, polynomial coefficient prediction, depth transformation, and derivative-regularized training objectives.

E1.justification: Both evaluate radar-camera metric depth estimation on nuScenes, ZJU-4DRadarCam, and View-of-Delft, including the same cross-dataset transfer and reduced-radar-density scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments. Both retain RadarNet, SparseBeatsDense, GET-UP, RadarCam-Depth, and TacoDepth comparisons, alongside the same supplementary depth-completion, regression, and adapter baselines.

E3.justification: Both retain MAE/RMSE evaluation at 50, 70, and 80 meters, the same dataset splits and cropping, 60-epoch training, and identical backbone, zero-shot, and radar-subsampling settings.

E4.justification: Polynomial-degree sensitivity, architecture and loss ablations, backbone comparisons, zero-shot transfer, radar-sparsity tests, monotonicity analysis, and qualitative case studies are unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix G in both versions reports Kendall's tau over 30 bootstrap samples and a two-sample t-test. No repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match, including supplementary results. For example, Table 1 reports identical POLAR nuScenes results at 80 meters: MAE 1407.8 mm and RMSE 3193.5 mm.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 and Appendix H's proposition, constructive proof, and corollary concerning global scale-and-shift limitations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about polynomial fitting, derivative regularization, superior accuracy across three datasets, and computational efficiency.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and result interpretations are identical. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning polynomial-degree tuning and stability of high-degree polynomial transformations.

D1.justification: Dataset processing, implementation settings, hardware descriptions, and reproducibility disclosures are unchanged. Appendix F retains the same learning rate, training schedule, and loss weights.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference entries, and research positioning are unchanged. Differences in bibliography placement result from text reflow, not added or removed references.

P1.justification: The acknowledgments add GITCC support through a KIAT grant, project P0028922, alongside the existing NSF acknowledgment. The arXiv version/date stamp is updated; scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The longer acknowledgment shifts reference text across columns and pages 9–12, and the first-page arXiv stamp changes. All figures, tables, captions, and supplementary layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v5 adds funding attribution, with accompanying reference reflow and an updated version stamp. The scientific argument, evidence, theory, limitations, and reproducibility information are unchanged, supporting no meaningful overall quality difference.
